# TSAFE-EVAL-01

Parent epic: #138

## Objective
Determine how reliably focused TypeSafe questions detect unsupported claims and insufficient assertions on Specflow examples before workflow adoption.

## Dependencies
Blocked by #139.

## Personas
- Interactive builder: wants one workflow and actionable observations tied to the agreed goal.
- Independent reviewer: needs the exact source/evidence and can disagree with a model judgment.
- Returning maintainer: needs reproducible records, explicit uncertainty and intact required gates.

## Scope boundaries
In Scope: local Node CLI helpers, durable JSON artifacts, native Claude/Codex workflow integration, documentation and executable CLI tests.
Not In Scope: replacing peer review, automatic acceptance/merge/deployment, autonomous command execution, a third conversational agent, database or browser UI changes, or adding jurisdiction support.
The project goal and original task acceptance remain authoritative. For Timebreez, accurate explainable entitlements/balances remain the ambition; unknown facts and unsupported jurisdictions stay explicit.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All mapped acceptance and negative-path CLI tests executed; full and contract suites pass.
- [ ] Live provider evidence is distinguished from mocked transport and cached replay; unavailable live verification is an explicit blocker to the live proof, not a passing result.
- [ ] No secrets in requests, logs, fixtures or committed evidence; only explicitly selected review material is sent externally.
- [ ] Native usage and troubleshooting documentation reflects delivered behaviour.
- [ ] Existing contracts, peer review, ownership, repair budgets and release gates remain enforced.
- [ ] Implementation/test/merge/deployment/customer-validation status recorded separately.

## Requirements
- REQ-EVAL-1 (MUST): Define separately versioned Choice questions for evidence support (supports/contradicts/insufficient) and assertion coverage (full/partial/none/insufficient). Supply exact criterion, bounded claim, selected assertion and relevant raw execution/source context. Code checks existence, hashes and execution counts; TypeSafe evaluates meaning, not arithmetic or required gate status.
- REQ-EVAL-2 (MUST): Create at least 50 explicitly labelled cases: at least 30 development and 20 held-out cases, split by originating task/failure family so paraphrases and related rounds do not leak across splits. Label origin as seeded or historical and include rationale/source references. Adjudicate labels before running held-out evaluation; do not treat reviewer agreement alone as truth.
- REQ-EVAL-3 (MUST): Cover valid support, wrong prominent value, element-presence-only assertion, partial coverage, required tests skipped/absent, failed command proving a separate fact, unrelated/missing evidence, unsupported deployment/jurisdiction claims and instruction-like text inside evidence. Include positive and negative examples for both questions.
- REQ-EVAL-4 (MUST): Provide a replay/evaluation command with a recorded dataset version/hash, fixed split, exact question and model versions, predictions and confusion matrices. Report unsupported-claim recall, false-alarm rate, coverage accuracy, insufficient/uncertain rate, actual calls/tokens, p50/p95 elapsed time and sample denominators. Report price/date separately if cost is estimated; never invent dollar totals.
- REQ-EVAL-5 (MUST): Compare with deterministic validation alone and available existing reviewer findings on the same labelled cases. Live provider evaluation and cached/offline regression runs must be separately named; tuning uses development cases only. Failed/absent provider calls stay unavailable and are counted, never dropped to inflate results.
- REQ-EVAL-6 (MUST): Keep adoption in shadow mode by default. Produce an explicit recommendation based on measured results and failure examples; any later advisory default or thresholds requires a recorded maintainer decision naming model/question/dataset versions. Do not claim a universal confidence threshold or production reliability from this small benchmark.

- REQ-EVAL-7 (MUST): The captured primitives documentation describes an approximately 32,000-token budget shared by state and questions; this is separate from our conservative 65,536-byte serialized-input cap and is not a bytes-to-tokens equivalence. Recheck provider limits when implementing; use recorded usage and explicit provider validation errors, not a guessed conversion. Batch all independent questions for the same bounded state into one request with a stable questionSetId/version. Questions see the same state and cannot consume each other's answers; only a genuine data dependency justifies a subsequent request. If a complete question set cannot fit, return an explicit limit/insufficient result or form separately recorded bounded states without silently dropping questions. Never import vendor cookbook speed/cost multipliers as measured Specflow benefits. Record per-case question count and actual request count; add a transport-level regression proving evidence-support and assertion-coverage questions on one state are sent together. This does not imply independent model errors. Keep aggregate evaluation reports private outside live duo rounds; during a round write only to the excluded run-state location specified by #141.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC-EVAL-1: Both question families return only their declared outcomes, with source identities and reproducible configuration.
- [ ] AC-EVAL-2: At least 50 labelled cases and a non-overlapping 30+/20+ development/held-out split exist; related paraphrases cannot cross the split.
- [ ] AC-EVAL-3: All listed failure classes and valid counterexamples are represented with rationale, and evaluation never treats missing context as support.
- [ ] AC-EVAL-4: A live run privately records complete per-case results and aggregate metrics with denominators; offline replay is separately labelled and reproducible.
- [ ] AC-EVAL-5: Unavailable calls remain visible in totals; comparison uses identical cases and no held-out tuning.
- [ ] AC-EVAL-6: The report explicitly states limitations and shadow/advisory recommendation; no metric or confidence score changes an acceptance or release gate.

- [ ] AC-EVAL-7: The two independent question families for a case are evaluated together; the report includes question/request counts and tests catch accidental serial per-question calls, without promising vendor benchmark speedups.

## Gherkin
```gherkin
Feature: TSAFE-EVAL-01
  Scenario: Evaluate held-out claims
    Given labels and split are frozen before inference
    When the live evaluation command runs
    Then per-case judgments, all failures and aggregate metrics are preserved
  Scenario: Missing execution evidence
    Given a claim lacks the required source material
    When the evidence-support check runs
    Then the result is insufficient or unavailable and never treated as a passing gate
```

## Architecture clarification from duo review
Node HTTP is retained after comparing the official `@typesafe-ai/sdk` (Node.js 20+, ESM/CommonJS and inferred TypeScript answer types). The SDK offers maintained transport, cancellation/timeouts and configurable retries; its default backoff is not our required one-attempt policy, but `retry.maxRetries: 0` can disable retries, so it is not inherently incompatible. For this small installed CLI adapter, native fetch avoids a new runtime dependency and gives direct control over the declared byte caps, abort handling and durable single-attempt records. Reconsider the SDK if maintaining this narrow adapter becomes more costly; do not grow a parallel general-purpose SDK. Python is not needed for the Node runtime. References: https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/javascript ; https://github.com/typesafe-ai/typesafe-sdk-js/blob/v0.6.0/src/client.ts ; https://docs.typesafe.ai/api#handling-rate-limits .

## PRD amendments
- REQ-EVAL-8 (MUST): Store live provider predictions and aggregate performance reports in an explicitly selected private directory outside tracked repository paths (default user-local Specflow data directory). Public source may contain synthetic fixtures and harness tests, but no generated provider benchmark results without applicable permission. Do not upload reports to GitHub automatically. Print report locations without printing provider metrics by default. Local private outputs are retained until the operator deletes them; document deletion.
- REQ-EVAL-9 (MUST): Add negation, irrelevant-context flooding, conflicting criteria, similar labels, unfamiliar inputs and repeat-run stability cases. Report probability calibration (multiclass Brier score and reliability bins) separately from accuracy/error versus confidence thresholds. Missing results remain in denominators. A small corpus does not establish production reliability.
- REQ-EVAL-10 (MUST): Compare same-case deterministic checks and available archived peer findings; missing peer baselines remain explicit. Measure incremental detections and review burden rather than required peer calls avoided. Promotion is a human-authored record with dataset/question/model identity, observed limitations and chosen mode; no automatic threshold promotion.
- [ ] AC-EVAL-8: An unsafe in-repository output destination is rejected, and default output is private; offline replay reports zero network calls and clearly names original result provenance.
- [ ] AC-EVAL-9: Robustness and repeat-run metrics, probability calibration and confidence-threshold accuracy are separately reported with denominators; changed models/questions require fresh qualification.
Mapping: REQ-EVAL-8/9/10 → tests/contracts/typesafe-evaluation.test.js and tests/contracts/typesafe-repair.test.js; I-TSAFE-004.

PRD: https://github.com/Hulupeep/Specflow/issues/138#issuecomment-5718728762

Context-limit clarification: Provider documentation is inconsistent: model limitations list 64k total and 32k state plus longest question; primitives describes approximately 32k shared. Keep the conservative 65,536-byte adapter cap, recheck provider validation, and never infer a token count from bytes.

## Pre-flight Findings

**simulation_status:** passed_with_warnings
**simulated_at:** 2026-09-17T17:43:41.402123+00:00
**scope:** ticket

### CRITICAL
None.
### P1
None.
### P2
Small labelled corpora do not establish production reliability. CLI implementation and live evidence remain required.

## Simulation Findings (proposed)

**simulated_at:** 2026-09-17T16:56:56+00:00

Four behavioural personas were routed through the draft (happy and divergent paths); this is paper simulation, not executed implementation.

- **Benchmark maintainer:** Freeze labels and split → run live → report metrics. Divergence: paraphrased copies cross splits; REQ-EVAL-2/5 and AC-EVAL-2/5 require family-level separation and no held-out tuning.
- **Builder with partial evidence:** Correct source-backed claim → supports. Divergence: card visible but balance unasserted, skipped tests or unsupported jurisdiction; REQ-EVAL-1/3 and AC-EVAL-3 require separate meaning checks and insufficient outcomes.
- **Returning analyst:** Replay exact recorded evaluation → identical historical report. Divergence: changed model or unavailable calls; REQ-EVAL-4/5 and AC-EVAL-4/5 require versioning and keep failed calls in denominators.
- **Skeptical reviewer:** Inspect labels and raw outputs → understand recommendation. Divergence: benchmark looks green despite tiny sample or schema-only baseline; REQ-EVAL-5/6 and AC-EVAL-6 require matched comparison, limitations and no automatic gate changes.

### Proposed additions
No new behavioural requirement is proposed: the divergent routes above are already covered by the cited draft requirements. The subsequent audit will add the missing typed record/interface shapes, traceability and ordered CLI journey mapping.

### Open questions
No blocking product question. Evaluation-derived thresholds and any advisory-default promotion remain explicitly deferred to the recorded evaluation/maintainer decision, not guessed during ticket creation.

## Specflow audit — gap analysis

Ticket type: non-UI CLI/agent-workflow feature.
PRESENT: parent/story ID, personas, scope, atomic requirements, positive/negative acceptance, Gherkin, DoD, dependency declarations.
MISSING: explicit data/interface applicability and typed shape, invariant references, contract/test mapping, ordered CLI journey success checks, ADR/reuse mapping. Only these missing sections are supplied below; original requirements are unchanged.

## Specflow Uplift: interfaces and executable verification mapping

### Data contract and interface
SQL/RLS: N/A, no database or tenant schema. Browser frontend/data-testid/Playwright: N/A, CLI workflow only. The proposed local JSON boundary is described below; this is an implementation deliverable, not a claim that an API or test already exists.

```typescript
export interface EvaluationCase {
  id: string; family: string; split: "development" | "held_out";
  origin: "seeded" | "historical"; criterion: string; claim: string;
  assertion: string | null; evidence: string[];
  expectedSupport: "supports" | "contradicts" | "insufficient";
  expectedCoverage: "full" | "partial" | "none" | "insufficient";
  labelRationale: string;
}
```

### Invariants referenced
Reserve these new non-colliding identifiers in the planned `docs/contracts/feature_typesafe_advisory.yml`, delivered by #139; no existing invariant ID is repurposed:
- I-TSAFE-001: bounded requests and durable records do not expose credentials or invent successful provider results.
- I-TSAFE-002: judgments and replay bind to exact input/snapshot/question/model identity; stale results cannot prove acceptance.
- I-TSAFE-003: advice cannot override owner fencing, independent review, required gates, finding closure or repair ceilings.
- I-TSAFE-004: evaluation retains unavailable outcomes, provenance and held-out separation; simulated/cached data is not called live proof.
Existing `docs/contracts/feature_specflow_project.yml`, `templates/contracts/security_defaults.yml`, and `templates/contracts/test_integrity_defaults.yml` remain applicable. #141/#142 also preserve the duo operational contract delivered by #135–#137; that prerequisite is not assumed present on main.

### SpecFlow contract and test mapping
Contract deliverable: `docs/contracts/feature_typesafe_advisory.yml` (YAML, not a Markdown contract).
- REQ-EVAL-1 → `tests/contracts/typesafe-evaluation.test.js` → named behavioural cases covering that requirement and its mapped acceptance above.
- REQ-EVAL-2 → `tests/contracts/typesafe-evaluation.test.js` → named behavioural cases covering that requirement and its mapped acceptance above.
- REQ-EVAL-3 → `tests/contracts/typesafe-evaluation.test.js` → named behavioural cases covering that requirement and its mapped acceptance above.
- REQ-EVAL-4 → `tests/contracts/typesafe-evaluation.test.js` → named behavioural cases covering that requirement and its mapped acceptance above.
- REQ-EVAL-5 → `tests/contracts/typesafe-evaluation.test.js` → named behavioural cases covering that requirement and its mapped acceptance above.
- REQ-EVAL-6 → `tests/contracts/typesafe-evaluation.test.js` → named behavioural cases covering that requirement and its mapped acceptance above.
Contract/journey test deliverable: `tests/contracts/typesafe-evaluation.test.js`; journey ID `J-TSAFE-EVAL`. Test doubles may isolate transport failure paths; labelled live proof is separately required by the DoD. No skip/stub can satisfy completion.

### CLI journey: J-TSAFE-EVAL
1. Load frozen labelled manifest → at least 30 development/20 held-out cases and no family overlap.
2. Run both question families → declared outcomes and per-case metadata saved.
3. Inject unavailable cases and inspect report → denominators retain failures and baselines use identical cases.
4. Replay → same historical predictions labelled offline; live report and recommendation remain separately identified.

Verification commands after implementation:
```sh
npx jest tests/contracts/typesafe-evaluation.test.js --runInBand --no-coverage
npm test -- --runInBand
npm test -- contracts --runInBand
```

### Relevant ADRs, reuse and surfaces
No ADR directory is present in this repository. Architecture decision: retain Node and the current helper/install machinery; HTTP adapter, no Python production dependency or new orchestration service. New files below are declared deliverables, not unresolved claims about current code.
- writes: `scripts/typesafe-evaluate.cjs`, `tests/fixtures/typesafe/`, `evidence/typesafe/`
- reads/reuses: `scripts/typesafe-client.cjs`
Dependencies are native GitHub blocked-by links and are also stated in the body. The shared files are implemented serially in the declared order to avoid conflicting writes.

Duo-review mapping addition: REQ-EVAL-7 → `tests/contracts/typesafe-evaluation.test.js` → complete same-state batch/request-count and snapshot-placement assertions.

The architecture clarification in the issue body records the explicit official JavaScript SDK comparison; it supplements the retained-Node decision here.

## Duo review correction and repeat Specflow simulation/audit

Claude's independent frozen-snapshot review returned changes_required. Corrections in this issue: TS-1 SDK rationale, TS-2 batching and measurable request counts, TS-4 offline report placement, TS-5 actual default-contract paths. Original acceptance and required release gates remain unchanged; new criteria add observable verification.

### Simulation Findings (proposed)
Four behavioural routes re-walked after correction:
- First-time Node user: evaluate SDK versus direct HTTP → both options are named, with configurable retry behaviour and explicit dependency/bounds tradeoffs.
- Repeated evaluator: send multiple independent questions → one complete-state request; dependent questions need an explicit later request; question IDs/versions and actual calls are retained.
- Returning maintainer: use an alias, then replay after a provider update → requested/reported identities remain distinct and the historical alias result cannot claim pinned/current verification.
- Cross-host reviewer: append TypeSafe advice during a paused review → excluded run-state writes leave the source fingerprint unchanged; actual source drift still invalidates the review.
No additional scope proposed; the five discovered gaps are addressed by the documented amendments. Optional run-wide spending limits, expanded corpus and alternate retry policy remain separate future evaluation decisions.

### Gap analysis and surgical uplift
Missing/incorrect items were the SDK comparison, batching requirement, alias-resolution guarantee, concrete storage location and actual default-contract paths. Corrected those specific passages and added only the related observable AC/test mappings. Interfaces now use requestedModel/reportedModel/modelPinned and questionSetId; earlier uplift comments were corrected to prevent conflicting sources of truth. SQL/RLS, frontend and Playwright remain N/A for this non-UI workflow.

### Pre-flight recheck
No CRITICAL or P1 remains in the amended specification on these routes: model identity is not assumed, token and byte bounds are distinct, complete question sets are required, record placement preserves snapshot integrity, and contract references resolve. This is preparation readiness only, pending Claude's re-review; no implementation or live TypeSafe integration is claimed.

## Simulation Findings (proposed)
Personas and distinct routes: first-time Claude user starts successfully / lacks credentials; returning operator resumes / exhausts provider budget; skeptical reviewer confirms support / rejects a confident false flag; evaluation maintainer runs held-out corpus / accidentally selects a public output path.
Concrete additions: missing-key explicit status; persistent call cap and two-failure suppression with owner recovery; evidence-backed flag rejection; private report destination rejection. These are now incorporated in the PRD amendments at the user's instruction. Happy and divergent routes remain executable acceptance deliverables, not executed product tests.

## Specflow audit — PRD reconciliation
Ticket type: non-UI CLI/agent-workflow feature (epic for #138).
Phase 1, gap analysis: parent/story, personas, scope, requirements, acceptance, Gherkin, DoD and dependency order PRESENT in body; data/interface applicability, typed interfaces, invariant references, contract/test mappings, ordered CLI journey, ADR/reuse PRESENT in existing uplift comments (epic composes child deliverables). New requirements map explicitly to existing test deliverables. SQL/RLS/browser testids are N/A: local CLI and JSON only.
Phase 2, surgical uplift: previous acceptance is retained. The PRD amendments supersede earlier report-publication wording. Private output defaults to the operator's home `.local/share/specflow/typesafe-evals`, permission 0700 for directories/0600 for records; custom outputs must be outside a Git worktree, symlink-free, and explicitly selected. Reports persist until explicitly deleted. Provider-budget recovery never resets consumed attempts. State fields: typesafe.mode (off/shadow/advisory), maxCalls (1..100, default20), calls, consecutiveFailures, changes (append-only owner actions). Optional environment-file credentials are loaded in the provider subprocess only; no raw values enter persisted state. Adapter unavailable reasons additionally include invalid_input and sensitive_input; integration-only suppression reasons include budget_exhausted, circuit_open and missing_selection. All added negative routes map to #139 client tests, #140 evaluation tests and #141 installed CLI tests. No new invariant IDs: reuse I-TSAFE-001..004 reserved by #139.
Phase 3, read-only pre-flight: dependency sequence 139→140→141→142 defined; #141's published prerequisite is b502c8d on feat/duo-goal-operations. No parallel writes. Existing contracts loaded: feature_preflight.yml (contract_meta), feature_specflow_project.yml (contract_meta); duo operations contract is defined by prerequisite #135–137. New TypeSafe contract/journeys are declared implementation deliverables, not claimed existing tests. Enum/shape amendments above reconcile prior interface comments. Pending→interrupted, single attempt, fresh snapshot, locks, budgets and private outputs cover partial failure. No UI scope, so Playwright is inapplicable; installed CLI journey must actually execute before completion.
CRITICAL: none. P1: none. P2: small labelled corpora support exploratory recommendations only; no production-reliability claim.
This is specification readiness, not implemented/tested/merged status.
